title: POC SDK edge-case & toolchain sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on SDK edge-case behavior for function/tool calling and structured output. Reviewed three failing scenarios, prioritized fixes for KV cache mismatch and function-arg serialization, agreed to run a 24-hour latency+error sweep on Redwood staging, and scheduled a deep-dive for private deployment feasibility.
topics: KV cache prefix mismatch with streaming responses
Structured output schema enforcement and fallbacks
Security: KMS integration and SSO concerns
Next-step staging load test and log handoff
action_items: Tom Alvarez - collect 5 failing request examples and post to shared folder - 2026-04-02
Jordan Patel - patch SDK v0.11.3 to handle null-typed function args and push PR - 2026-04-01
Maya Chen - share staging ingress logs and suggested perf spreadsheet - 2026-03-31
Aisha Rahman - confirm compliance checklist items for SOC2 scoping call - 2026-04-06
next_steps: Run 24hr staging sweep with 1k simulated users (Redwood to run, customer to provide synthetic prompts)
Customer to provide 5 repro cases and a data sample for structured output mismatch
Schedule private-deployment feasibility deep-dive week of 2026-04-05
Redwood to send updated SDK build and quickstart snippet via email
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Aisha (Bluebird Eng Lead), Tom (Bluebird ML), Priya (Bluebird PM)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we've got about 45 minutes, quick agenda: reproduce cases, patch status, staging sweep, next steps.
[00:18] Aisha: yep, that sounds good, thanks Maya. quick note, Tom's got the repros in the sheet but also we'll show one live if that's okay.
[00:28] Tom: yeah i uploaded three examples, two are structured-output mismatches and one is a function call where args become strings, like "123" instead of number.
[00:40] Jordan: got it, that one sounds like a serialization edge. in our last build we relaxed strict typing for function args to accept strings, but i think it broke the downstream parser.
[00:52] Priya: just to add, for product success we need deterministic outputs for billing events, so that function-call schema mismatch is a blocker.
[01:05] Maya: okay, priority is the function-call arg types, second is the KV cache mismatch you mentioned, Tom, can you walk us through that?
[01:18] Tom: sure, so when we enable streaming responses and prefix caching, occasionally the KV cache lookup returns an older token sequence — we see duplicated partial answers. it seems tied to our batching window and long-polling. sometimes the SDK retries with a different session id and then the cache key doesn't line up.
[01:39] Jordan: that sounds like session-id entropy, we added session scoping last month but maybe the SDK isn't passing the runtime session hash in the streaming handshake.
[01:52] Aisha: also thought it could be a race when we rehydrate state after a network hiccup, we saw it during our spike test.
[02:03] Jordan: could be, ok quick note, we patched the SDK to include a session token but only in non-streaming paths — my bad.
[02:14] Maya: alright, that's actionable. Jordan, can you add the session token into the streaming handshake and cut a patch?
[02:20] Jordan: yes, i'll do that, i'll also add a fallback where if the cache key mismatches we do a short suffix compare before returning old output.
[02:31] Tom: would that increase latency? we have a 200ms SLO on median response for that route.
[02:37] Jordan: minor, maybe +15ms on the worst case, but we can short-circuit the path if mismatch probability is low.
[02:45] Priya: on latency, we saw spikes during burst batching — any suggestions on batching windows? we've got 50ms default.
[02:55] Maya: if you're seeing burst spikes, 50ms may be long for P50 sensitive routes. recommended starting point is 20ms with dynamic batching off for critical billing calls. you can keep batching on for low-priority analytics.
[03:10] Aisha: ok we'll try 20ms for the billing endpoint. what's the recommended quantization profile? some of our models are T4-backed, wondering about accuracy loss.
[03:21] Jordan: for T4 we recommend 4-bit quant for embeddings and 8-bit for generative tasks; the accuracy delta for your prompt set looked acceptable in our preview tests but we can run an eval on your test prompts.
[03:33] Tom: let's do that, also one of the failing cases was a function call that returned an empty tool payload when tool invocation included nested arrays.
[03:43] Jordan: nested arrays is a known gap in the current SDK serializer. the SDK flattens arrays if depth>2 due to a legacy helper.
[03:54] Priya: wait it flattens? that seems risky. we rely on nested lists for multi-item claims.
[04:01] Jordan: agreed, it's a bug. quick fix is to remove the flatten helper and use JSON.stringify for nested args then parse on the runtime side. i'm on it.
[04:09] Maya: great, patch that and we'll push a hotfix.
[04:14] Aisha: security question — if we do private deployment, how does KMS and audit logging work? we need key ownership for patient data.
[04:24] Maya: for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; keys never leave your VPC and we write audit logs to your syslog/S3 with tenant IDs. we can walk through the SOC2 artifacts in the deep-dive.
[04:37] Priya: will that require a separate contract?
[04:40] Maya: slightly different licensing yes, we'll include private deployment fees and support tier. i'll send the pricing sheet.
[04:48] Tom: on the repros, i can show one now?
[04:52] Maya: please do, share your screen.
[05:00] Tom: (screen share noise) here, this call sends payload with function name "bill_event" and args: {"amount": 123, "items": [[1,2],[3,4]]}. SDK sends back args as {"amount": "123", "items": [1,2,3,4]} so items flattened and amount coerced.
[05:23] Jordan: yep that's the flatten helper + type coercion, we'll change serializer to maintain numeric types and nested arrays.
[05:32] Aisha: will that be backwards compatible for us?
[05:35] Jordan: it will be a minor semver bump but we can support old behavior behind a feature flag for a short period.
[05:43] Priya: ok feature flag would be safer.
[05:46] Maya: note: Jordan will branch feature-flag support and release.
[05:50] Tom: another rare case — structured output validation fails when keys reorder, our schema validator is strict about property order in one internal stage.
[06:01] Jordan: JSON object ordering should not matter, sounds like your internal validator may be using a line-based comparator. we recommend using schema-based comparison (JSON Schema) or canonicalization before diffs.
[06:14] Aisha: we actually do a line diff to detect drift in billing templates, maybe that's the root cause.
[06:20] Maya: ok we'll send a short doc on canonicalization and schema enforcement patterns.
[06:26] Priya: can Redwood add a structured-output example in the SDK quickstart showing canonicalization?
[06:31] Maya: yes, i'll add a step and an example snippet.
[06:35] Jordan: quick engineering note: during the last pilot we observed a memory bump on the host when batch sizes reached 64 and sequence len average >512; we added a stream-eviction routine to prevent GC thrash, but your prompts are sometimes long.
[06:52] Tom: our prompts do hit 700 tokens sometimes with system message. any guidance?
[06:57] Jordan: for long prompts we suggest pinned KV cache for the session and a lower batch size, e.g., 8-16, and use prefix caching to avoid re-encoding common system messages.
[07:10] Aisha: prefix caching seemed to be working but we saw mismatch, which you mentioned may be session keys.
[07:16] Maya: Jordan will update SDK for streaming session token, Jordan: estimate?
[07:20] Jordan: i can have a patch tomorrow, and a build by Friday.
[07:24] Maya: great. moving on to staging sweep — we propose Redwood runs a 24hr sweep with our synthetic prompt set, telemetry collection includes latency P50/P95, error rates, and cache hit ratio. can you confirm the telemetry hooks?
[07:38] Tom: yes we'll provide the prompts and some sticky session ids. do you need wire logs?
[07:43] Jordan: logs are useful; please mask PHI before upload. we'll provide a secure S3 bucket with KMS encryption and short-lived credentials.
[07:53] Aisha: we'll scrub PHI and generate synthetic users, timeline is we can provide prompts by end of day tomorrow.
[07:59] Maya: perfect. we'll schedule the sweep start 2026-04-01 00:00 UTC.
[08:05] Priya: switching to tool fallback logic — if a tool call fails we want graceful degradation to a simple summary, not an empty payload. is there a Redwood pattern?
[08:16] Jordan: yes, we recommend a fallback chain: 1) retry immediate once, 2) if tool returns error return structured error object with human-friendly summary and a trace id, 3) if configured, call alternative tool or model variant.
[08:33] Tom: good, that trace id will help us reconcile billing events.
[08:38] Priya: how about cost controls during burst? we saw a 5x cost jump in earlier test.
[08:44] Maya: enable per-route cost caps and a throttle policy; also you can route to a lower-cost model variant for non-critical requests. we'll share recommended policy configs.
[08:55] Aisha: okay, will review.
[08:58] Jordan: on benchmarks, we need one more data point: your 95th perc latency with 20ms batching and batch size 8 vs 50ms/32. i can run quick sim and post numbers.
[09:09] Tom: please do. also, are there any changes needed for our CI to support SDK update? we run end-to-end tests in a dockerized runner.
[09:18] Jordan: SDK is pure JS/Py, should be a drop-in, no infra change, but if you use pinned hashes we will provide the new build hash.
[09:26] Priya: ok that's fine.
[09:28] Maya: quick recap for next steps: Jordan patch serializer + streaming token, Tom posts repros, Redwood runs staging sweep, Maya shares pricing and private-deploy checklist, schedule deep-dive.
[09:41] Aisha: can we book the deep-dive now? week of Apr 5 we have Thurs open.
[09:46] Maya: Thursday Apr 8 16:00 UTC works for us, i'll send invite.
[09:50] Priya: one last question — if we go Private, what's the SLA for failover? we need cross-region support.
[09:58] Maya: Private supports regional failover with optional multi-AZ; cross-region is an add-on with replication. Jordan can ping infra for details.
[10:09] Jordan: i'll follow up with infra and include replication RTO/RPO numbers.
[10:14] Tom: thanks everyone, we'll get the repros in by tomorrow.
[10:20] Maya: thanks team, we'll follow up on the action items and share the quick links, see you next week.

(Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions, filler words, and speaker overlaps typical of call records.)
